name: Istanbul
description: Straddling the Bosphorus between Europe and Asia, Istanbul was capital of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires. Its historic peninsula of Sultanahmet holds many of the city's greatest monuments within walking distance of each other.

name: Cappadocia
description: A high plateau in central Anatolia where volcanic ash has eroded into cones, pillars and valleys. People have carved homes, churches and entire underground cities into its soft rock for well over a thousand years.

name: Pamukkale
description: A village in south-western Turkey below a hillside of white travertine terraces formed by mineral-rich hot springs. The Roman spa city of Hierapolis spreads across the plateau above.

name: Selçuk
description: A small, friendly market town near the Aegean coast and the gateway to ancient Ephesus. Its hilltop castle and the lone column of the Temple of Artemis are within easy reach.

name: Dubai
description: A global city of record-breaking towers, luxury hotels and beaches, grown from a small pearling and trading port on Dubai Creek. Its desert begins less than an hour from Downtown.

name: Abu Dhabi
description: The capital of the UAE, calmer and greener than Dubai, set on an island with the cultural district of Saadiyat alongside. It is home to some of the region's most important religious and cultural buildings.

name: AlUla
description: An oasis valley in north-western Saudi Arabia, framed by sandstone cliffs and dotted with rock formations and ancient inscriptions. It was a staging post on the incense route for more than two thousand years.

name: Riyadh
description: Saudi Arabia's fast-changing capital sits on the Najd plateau in the centre of the peninsula. Beyond its modern towers lie the restored mud-brick heart of Diriyah and the dramatic Tuwaiq escarpment.

name: Red Sea Coast
description: Saudi Arabia's western coast faces some of the healthiest coral reefs in the Red Sea. A new generation of low-density island and desert resorts is opening along its lagoons.

name: Kuala Lumpur
description: Malaysia's capital is a green, modern city of towers, mosques, temples and superb street food. It grew from a 19th-century tin-mining settlement where two rivers meet.

name: Langkawi
description: An archipelago of around a hundred islands in the Andaman Sea, close to the Thai border. Rainforest, mangroves and ancient limestone give it the status of a UNESCO Global Geopark.

name: George Town
description: The capital of Penang island, founded as a British trading post in 1786. Its streets of shophouses, clan houses and temples are among Asia's best-preserved, and its food is famous across the region.

name: Cameron Highlands
description: A cool hill station in the Titiwangsa range, about 1,500 metres above sea level. Tea estates, strawberry farms and mossy cloud forest make it a restful contrast to the lowlands.

name: Bangkok
description: Thailand's capital unfolds along the Chao Phraya River, where royal palaces and temples stand near riverside hotels and busy markets. It is a city best explored by boat as much as by road.

name: Chiang Mai
description: The cultural capital of northern Thailand, founded in 1296, with a moated old city full of temples. Forested mountains rise just beyond its western edge.

name: Phuket
description: Thailand's largest island, on the Andaman coast, with fine beaches and a wide choice of resorts. It is the main gateway to the limestone islands of Phang Nga Bay.

name: Krabi
description: A province on the Andaman coast known for towering limestone cliffs, clear water and scattered islands. Its coastline around Ao Nang and Railay is among the most striking in Thailand.

name: London
description: The capital of the United Kingdom, a city of royal ceremony, world-class museums, parks and theatres. Two thousand years of history are layered along the River Thames.

name: Edinburgh
description: Scotland's capital, built across hills and ridges between a castle on volcanic rock and the royal palace of Holyroodhouse. Its medieval Old Town and Georgian New Town are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Isle of Skye
description: The largest island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast, linked to the mainland by a bridge. Its jagged mountains, sea cliffs and small crofting villages have a rare, wild beauty.

name: Bath
description: A graceful city in Somerset built around natural hot springs, famous for its Roman baths and honey-coloured Georgian crescents. The whole city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Paris
description: France's capital on the Seine, a city of wide boulevards, café terraces and world-class museums, best explored on foot between its neighbourhoods and riverside quays.

name: Versailles
description: A stately town south-west of Paris, built around the royal palace and its gardens, and an easy half-hour to forty minutes by train from the city centre.

name: Normandy
description: A green region of orchards, dairy farms and dramatic tidal coast in north-western France, known for its abbeys, cider and Second World War history.

name: French Riviera
description: The Mediterranean coast between Nice and the Italian border, where hilltop villages look down on turquoise bays, yachts and Belle Époque villas.

name: Rome
description: The Eternal City, where ancient ruins, Baroque piazzas and the Vatican sit within walking distance of one another, and every street carries some layer of history.

name: Florence
description: The compact capital of Tuscany and cradle of the Renaissance, with Brunelleschi's dome, Medici palaces and galleries filled with masterpieces along the Arno.

name: Venice
description: A city of canals and palazzi built across more than a hundred small islands in a lagoon, where boats replace cars and every journey happens on foot or by water.

name: Amalfi Coast
description: A steep stretch of coastline south of Naples, with pastel villages stacked above the sea, lemon terraces and a winding cliff road between Positano, Amalfi and Ravello.

name: Granada
description: An Andalusian city below the Sierra Nevada, the last seat of Muslim rule in Spain, with the Alhambra above and the white lanes of the Albaicín opposite.

name: Barcelona
description: Catalonia's seaside capital, known for Gaudí's modernist buildings, the medieval Gothic Quarter and a relaxed Mediterranean way of life.

name: Seville
description: The capital of Andalusia, a city of orange trees, tiled courtyards and flamenco, with one of the largest Gothic cathedrals in the world.

name: Madrid
description: Spain's elegant capital, home to the royal palace, leafy Retiro Park and three great art museums within a short walk of each other.

name: Zermatt
description: A car-free Alpine village at the foot of the Matterhorn, with chalets, fine hotels and railways and cable cars leading to high glaciers.

name: Jungfrau Region
description: The Bernese Oberland around Interlaken, Grindelwald and Wengen, overlooked by the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau and threaded with mountain railways.

name: Lucerne
description: A graceful lakeside city in central Switzerland, with a medieval old town, painted façades and steamers crossing to the surrounding mountains.

name: Athens
description: Greece's capital, where the Acropolis rises above a busy modern city of neighbourhood tavernas, rooftop bars and excellent museums.

name: Santorini
description: A crescent-shaped volcanic island in the Cyclades, its white villages perched on cliffs above a flooded caldera.

name: Meteora
description: A landscape of towering sandstone pillars above the town of Kalambaka in Thessaly, crowned by Eastern Orthodox monasteries.

name: Mykonos
description: A lively Cycladic island of whitewashed lanes, windmills and beaches, and the departure point for boats to ancient Delos.

name: Kyoto
description: Japan's imperial capital for more than a thousand years, with around 1,600 Buddhist temples, hundreds of shrines, traditional wooden townhouses and refined gardens.

name: Tokyo
description: A vast, orderly metropolis where old temple districts and quiet gardens sit beside some of the world's most modern neighbourhoods.

name: Hakone
description: A hot-spring mountain area south-west of Tokyo, with volcanic valleys, a lake and, on clear days, views of Mount Fuji.

name: Bavarian Alps
description: The southern edge of Bavaria, where lakes and meadows rise into the Alps. The villages of Schwangau and Hohenschwangau sit below King Ludwig II's castles.

name: Berlin
description: Germany's capital, spread wide along the River Spree. Its museums, memorials and restored boulevards trace Prussian ambition, division by the Wall and reunification in 1990.

name: Rhine Valley
description: The Upper Middle Rhine between Bingen and Koblenz, a steep gorge of vineyards, castles and wine villages. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2002.

name: Black Forest
description: A wooded upland range in south-west Germany, stretching from Baden-Baden towards the Swiss border. Known for spa towns, walking trails, farmhouses and cuckoo clocks.

name: Vienna
description: Austria's capital and the former seat of the Habsburg Empire. Palaces, opera, museums and coffee houses fill a city that is walkable and quietly grand.

name: Salzburg
description: A baroque city on the Salzach river, overlooked by a medieval fortress. Mozart's birthplace and host of the Salzburg Festival every summer.

name: Hallstatt
description: A small lakeside village in the Salzkammergut, pressed between the Hallstätter See and steep mountains. Salt has been mined here for thousands of years.

name: Lisbon
description: Portugal's capital, built across hills above the Tagus estuary. The riverside district of Belém holds the city's great monuments to the Age of Discovery.

name: Sintra
description: A hill town about 40 minutes west of Lisbon, where royal palaces and romantic estates sit in misty forest. Its cultural landscape is UNESCO-listed.

name: Porto
description: Portugal's second city, stacked above the Douro river and linked to the port-wine lodges of Vila Nova de Gaia. The gateway to the Douro Valley wine region.

name: Algarve
description: Portugal's southern coast, facing the Atlantic. Golden limestone cliffs, sea caves and fishing towns run from Sagres in the west towards the Spanish border.

name: Amsterdam
description: The Dutch capital, arranged around a ring of 17th-century canals. Gabled merchants' houses, major museums and bicycles define its compact centre.

name: South Holland
description: The province south-west of Amsterdam, covering bulb fields, polders and the cities of Rotterdam, The Hague and Leiden. Flat, green and threaded with waterways.

name: Dubrovnik
description: A walled city on Croatia's far southern coast. Its limestone streets, churches and fortifications have been UNESCO-listed since 1979.

name: Plitvice Lakes
description: Croatia's best-known national park, in the forested interior between Zagreb and Zadar. Terraced lakes are joined by waterfalls and wooden walkways.

name: Split
description: Dalmatia's largest city, grown up inside and around a Roman emperor's palace. The main ferry hub for the central Adriatic islands.

name: Hvar
description: A long, sunny island off the Dalmatian coast. Known for its Venetian-era harbour town, lavender fields, vineyards and nearby islets.

name: Beijing
description: China's capital for most of the last six centuries, home to the Forbidden City, grand imperial parks and hutong lanes, with the Great Wall within a short drive to the north.

name: Xi'an
description: Former capital of thirteen dynasties and the eastern end of the Silk Road, with intact Ming city walls, a historic Muslim quarter and the Terracotta Army on its outskirts.

name: Guilin
description: A city in southern Guangxi set among limestone karst peaks, and the starting point for cruises down the Li River to the riverside town of Yangshuo.

name: Bali
description: A Hindu island within mostly Muslim Indonesia, known for temple ceremonies, terraced rice fields around Ubud and dramatic cliffs on the southern Bukit peninsula.

name: Yogyakarta
description: Central Java's cultural capital, home to a working sultan's palace, batik workshops and gamelan music, and the base for visiting Borobudur and Prambanan.

name: Labuan Bajo
description: A harbour town on the western tip of Flores and the gateway to Komodo National Park, where traditional phinisi boats set out for the islands.

name: Ha Long Bay
description: A bay in northeast Vietnam scattered with limestone islands, best explored by overnight cruise, with the quieter waters of Lan Ha Bay to its south.

name: Hoi An
description: A former trading port on the Thu Bon River whose lantern-hung old town, tailors and nearby beaches make it the easiest place in Vietnam to slow down.

name: Hanoi
description: Vietnam's capital, a city of lakes, tree-lined French-era boulevards and a dense old merchant quarter where street food is part of daily life.

name: Hue
description: The seat of the Nguyen emperors from 1802 to 1945, set on the Perfume River with a walled citadel and royal tombs in the hills beyond.

name: Seoul
description: A capital of ten million people where five Joseon palaces, traditional hanok neighbourhoods and mountain trails sit among glass towers and late-night food streets.

name: Jeju Island
description: A volcanic island off Korea's southern coast, shaped by Hallasan, the country's highest peak, with lava tubes, crater cones and a rugged coastline.

name: Gyeongju
description: Capital of the Silla kingdom for nearly a thousand years, often called a museum without walls for its royal burial mounds, temples and ruins.

name: Marina Bay
description: Singapore's waterfront centre, built largely on reclaimed land, where Marina Bay Sands, Gardens by the Bay and the colonial civic district meet around the water.

name: Sentosa
description: A resort island just off Singapore's southern shore with beaches, theme parks, golf and several of the city's quieter luxury hotels.

name: North Malé Atoll
description: The atoll closest to the capital and the international airport, home to many of the Maldives' established resorts, surf breaks and classic dive sites.

name: Baa Atoll
description: A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in the northwest of the country, known for healthy reefs and the seasonal manta ray gatherings at Hanifaru Bay.

name: Ari Atoll
description: A large atoll west of Malé with some of the country's best diving, including a marine protected area where whale sharks are seen all year.

name: Sigiriya
description: A village in the Cultural Triangle, the dry central plains that hold Sri Lanka's ancient capitals, cave temples and great reservoirs.

name: Kandy
description: The last royal capital of Sri Lanka's kings, set around a lake in the central hills and home to the island's most revered Buddhist temple.

name: Ella
description: A small town in the southern hill country, surrounded by tea estates and ridges, and one of the most scenic stops on the upland railway.

name: Galle
description: A port on the southwest coast whose walled fort encloses a living town of Dutch-era houses, churches, boutique hotels and cafés.

name: Tbilisi
description: Georgia's capital climbs the banks of the Mtkvari river, with balconied wooden houses, sulphur baths and a fortress above the old town.

name: Mtskheta
description: The ancient capital and spiritual heart of Georgia, set where the Aragvi and Mtkvari rivers meet, about 20 kilometres north of Tbilisi.

name: Greater Caucasus
description: Georgia's high mountain country, from Kazbegi on the Georgian Military Road to the tower villages of Upper Svaneti in the north-west.

name: Kakheti
description: Georgia's eastern wine region, a broad valley of vineyards and monasteries beneath the Caucasus, centred on the hill town of Sighnaghi.

name: Baku
description: The Caspian capital of Azerbaijan, where a walled old city sits beside a long seafront boulevard and some of the Caucasus's boldest modern architecture.

name: Gobustan
description: A dry, rocky stretch of coast south-west of Baku, known for ancient rock carvings and the bubbling mud volcanoes nearby.

name: Sheki
description: A historic silk town in the forested foothills of the Greater Caucasus, with caravanserais, craft workshops and an eighteenth-century khan's palace.

name: Gabala
description: A mountain resort town in northern Azerbaijan, with forests, lakes, waterfalls and cable cars into the Greater Caucasus.

name: Samarkand
description: Timur's capital and the most famous Silk Road city, with monumental tiled squares, mausoleums and observatory ruins from the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries.

name: Bukhara
description: A compact, walkable holy city of mosques, madrasas, trading domes and a citadel, lived in continuously for more than two thousand years.

name: Khiva
description: A desert oasis town in western Uzbekistan whose walled inner city survives almost complete, a short drive from Urgench.
